title: ‘प्रिय मौनता’ कविता सङ्ग्रहमा कामसूत्रको प्रभाव [The effect of Kamasutra on 'Priya Maunta' poetry collection]
nepali: प्रस्तुत अनुसन्धनात्मक लेखमा नेत्र एटमको ‘प्रिय मौनता’ कविता सङ्ग्रहलाई पाठका रुपमा लिई त्यसमा प्रयुक्त कामशास्त्रीय मान्यताका शृङ्गारिकता र काम एवम् मन सिद्धान्तका आधारमा विश्लेषण र मूल्याङ्कन गरेर उक्त कविता सङ्ग्रहमा कामसूत्रको प्रभाव केकस्तो छ भनेर निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ । प्रेम, प्रणय र आकर्षणलाई मुख्य विषय बनाइएको यस कविता सङ्ग्रहको प्रणयको प्यासन र प्रमुदित प्रकृति खण्डमा यौन सन्दर्भहरू प्रशस्त रुपमा आएका छन् । शृङ्गारिकताअन्तर्गत विभाव, अनुभाव, व्यभिचारीभाव र स्थायीभावका साथै काम एवम् मनको सन्दर्भ पनि सशक्त रुपमा प्रयोग भएको छ । ‘म’ पात्र अर्थात कविले आफ्नो कल्पनाका माध्यमबाट विभिन्न प्रेमिकाहरूसँग प्रेमसुख प्राप्त गरेको सन्दर्भमा सम्भोग शृङ्गारको प्रयोग भएको, कवि पात्र प्रेमिकाहरूसँग बिछोडिनुपरेको सन्दर्भमा विप्रलम्व शृङ्गारको प्रयोग भएको, ‘म’पात्र वा कविले यौनसुखको कल्पना गरेको सन्दर्भमा शृङ्गार सामग्रीका साथै प्राक्क्रियाको प्रयोग भएको, प्रेमप्राप्ति हुँदा मन आनन्दित भएको तर प्रेमिकासँग वियोग हुँदा मन सुखी नभएको प्रसङ्गलाई विषय बनाइएको यस उपन्यासमा वात्सायनको कामसूत्रको प्रभाव रहेको छ भन्ने निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ । [Writers In the research article presented by Netra Atom's 'Priya Maunta' poetry collection as a text, by analyzing and evaluating the beauty of kamasastra principles used in it and the effect of Kamasutra on the said poetry collection It has been concluded that. Love, romance and attraction are the main themes of this collection of poems, and there are plenty of sexual references in the passion of romance and the popular nature section. In the context of beauty, feelings, feelings, promiscuity and permanence, as well as work and mind, have been strongly used. 'M' character i.e. the poet using his imagination to have sexual pleasure with different girlfriends. It has been concluded that Vatsayana's Kamasutra has been influenced in this novel, which deals with the case of being happy but not happy when parting with a girlfriend.]
american_english: In the present research article, by taking Netra Atom's poetry collection 'Priya Maunata' as a text and analyzing and evaluating it on the basis of the eroticism of the kamashastra principles used in it and the theory of desire and mind, a conclusion has been drawn as to what kind of effect the Kamasutra has on that poetry collection. Love, romance and attraction have been made the main subjects of this poetry collection, and sexual references have appeared abundantly in the passion of romance and the promudit nature section. Under eroticism, vibhava, anubhava, vyabhicharibhava and sthayibhava, along with the context of desire and mind, have also been used forcefully. In the context where the 'I' character, that is, the poet, obtains erotic pleasure with various girlfriends through his imagination, shringara of union has been used; in the context where the poet character has to be separated from the girlfriends, vipralambha shringara has been used; in the context where the 'I' character or poet imagines sexual pleasure, shringara material along with process has been used; and the matter that the mind becomes delighted when love is obtained but the mind is not happy when separated from the girlfriend has been made the subject — in this novel it has been concluded that there is an influence of Vatsayana's Kamasutra.

informal_english: Right, so in this research piece they took Netra Atom's poetry collection 'Priya Maunata' as the text and analysed and evaluated it on the basis of the erotic beauty of the kamashastra principles used in it and the theory of desire and mind, working out what kind of effect the Kamasutra has on that collection. Love, romance and attraction are the main subjects, and sexual references come up plenty in the passion-of-romance and promudit-nature sections. Under eroticism they've used vibhava, anubhava, vyabhicharibhava and sthayibhava, plus the desire-and-mind context, quite forcefully. Where the 'I' character — the poet — gets erotic pleasure with various girlfriends through his imagination, they've used shringara of union; where the poet character has to part from the girlfriends, vipralambha shringara; where the 'I' character or poet imagines sexual pleasure, shringara material plus process; and the bit about the mind being delighted when love is gained but not happy when parted from the girlfriend — that's all made the subject, and in this novel they've concluded there's an influence of Vatsayana's Kamasutra.
translator_notes: The Nepali source calls the work 'उपन्यास' (novel) although the title is a poetry collection; translated literally as 'novel'. The trailing English gloss in square brackets in the source was not used as a substitute for translating the Nepali.
